newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Duma asked to reject law on oil reserves.
newsitem.headline: Russia Duma asked to reject law on oil reserves.

text.p: Russian parliamentarians said on Thursday they would asked deputies to reject a list of huge oil reserves to be developed on a production-sharing basis, dealing a blow to foreign investors in the energy sector.

Members of the audit chamber of the Federation Council (upper house of parliament) told a news conference that they had reviewed the list and would recommend that the State Duma (lower house) reject it next month.

Duma deputies have said the lower house is likely to reject the law. Rejection would hamper existing preliminary, billion-dollar production-sharing agreements with foreign investors and delay new ones.
An audit chamber news release said it recommended that three of the biggest reserves proposed for production sharing -- Priobsk, Samotlor and Krasnoleninskoe -- be developed on such a basis.
But it said it would recommend that no tenders open to foreign investors be held for Samotlor and Krasnoleninskoye.
Amoco Corp of the United States and Russian oil company YUKOS have a preliminary agreement to develop Priobsk.
The two plan to spend $50 billion to tap the field, one of Russia's largest, on a production-sharing basis if the necessary laws are in place, including the reserves list law.

The chamber release said it would be "expedient to establish the limits of the production-sharing agreement (for this field), as well as to examine the need to have federal laws confirm the agreement."

Duma Deputy Yuri Boldyrev, who is deputy chairman of the audit chamber, said the chamber had rejected the list of about 250 oilfields totalling 38 percent of Russia's oil reserves, because government officials had not proven it would be prudent to develop them on a production-sharing basis.
He said it would make more sense for Russia to present 10 or 15 fields a year.
Boldyrev condemned government, finance and economy ministry officials for failing to present what he said was the most basic financial information on plans to develop the reserves.
